narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic situation and determined that there’s a **24% chance** you might not pass your final year. While this isn’t a certainty, it’s high enough that your school has decided you should take extra remedial courses to help you succeed. Think of it like a warning sign—your current path has some risks, but with support, you can still reach your goals.

The decision isn’t based on random guesswork. Three key factors stood out in shaping this prediction, and understanding them can help you adjust your approach.

First, the **reason you chose this school**—you prioritized its reputation over other factors like proximity or course fit. While reputation is important, it doesn’t guarantee your success if you’re not fully engaged. Most students who pass focus more on the course itself, suggesting that your motivation might need a stronger connection to your own academic goals.

Second, your **family relationships** are described as "good," which is positive, but not as strong as "very good." Strong family support often correlates with better academic outcomes, as students with close-knit families tend to have more encouragement and stability. Even small improvements in communication or involvement from your family could make a meaningful difference.

Finally, the model noticed that you **haven’t had any past class failures**, which is actually a protective factor—it suggests you’re capable of doing the work. However, the absence of failures alone isn’t enough if other areas, like study habits or focus, aren’t optimized. Right now, you’re studying **2-5 hours a week**, which is below what many successful students put in (most study **5-10 hours**). Even small increases in dedicated study time could shift the odds in your favor.

The good news? This isn’t a permanent label—it’s a call to action. Remedial courses are designed to give you targeted help, whether that’s strengthening weak areas, improving time management, or building confidence. Use this as a chance to reassess: Are there small changes you can make to your routine, support system, or mindset? The model’s message is clear: **You’re on the right track, but with a little more focus and support, you can turn this 24% risk into a success story.**
